description: Enforces TLS 1.3 as the minimum protocol version for all TLS connections, rejecting TLS 1.2 and below at the handshake layer. TLS 1.3 eliminates entire attack classes present in earlier versions: CBC mode ciphers are removed (preventing BEAST, Lucky13 padding oracle attacks), renegotiation is removed (preventing renegotiation-based attacks), only AEAD cipher suites are available (AES-128-GCM, AES-256-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305), forward secrecy is mandatory via ephemeral ECDHE/X25519 key exchange (no static RSA key transport), and the server certificate is encrypted during the handshake. Enforcement is configured at the service level (nginx ssl_protocols, Apache SSLProtocol, Tomcat sslEnabledProtocols), reverse proxy level, or system crypto policy level (update-crypto-policies on RHEL). Does not protect applications using custom TLS implementations that bypass system crypto libraries (Go's crypto/tls, Java's JSSE, custom-compiled OpenSSL). Compatibility constraint: legacy clients and embedded devices that do not support TLS 1.3 will fail to connect.

cvss_vector_impacts.rationale: Without TLS 1.3 enforcement, a network attacker can force protocol downgrade to TLS 1.2 or lower using well-tooled attacks: POODLE forces TLS 1.0 fallback to exploit CBC padding, DROWN exploits SSLv2 to decrypt TLS sessions, and FREAK/Logjam force export-grade key exchange. With TLS 1.3 enforcement, the server rejects any handshake below 1.3 — the downgrade path does not exist. Additionally, TLS 1.3 mandates forward secrecy via ephemeral key exchange, so even if a server's long-term private key is later compromised, past sessions cannot be retroactively decrypted. The attacker must perform a real-time MitM against AEAD ciphers with ephemeral keys, which requires fundamentally different (and harder) cryptographic attacks than exploiting known protocol weaknesses

verification.method: Verify TLS 1.2 is rejected and TLS 1.3 is the minimum accepted protocol version

commands.command: openssl s_client -connect <host>:<port> -tls1_2 </dev/null 2>&1 | grep -ci 'handshake failure\|alert protocol_version\|no protocols available'

relationships.rationale: TLS 1.3 enforcement rejects all handshakes below version 1.3 — the server cannot negotiate down to TLS 1.2, 1.1, 1.0, or SSLv3 because the protocol version check occurs before cipher negotiation. Downgrade attacks (POODLE, DROWN) have no lower-version endpoint to target.

TLS 1.3 exclusively supports AEAD cipher suites (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305) and mandates ephemeral key exchange — CBC mode ciphers, RC4, static RSA key transport, and renegotiation do not exist in the protocol specification. Broken algorithms cannot be selected because they are absent from the TLS 1.3 cipher suite definitions.
